new_entities.name: Nitrate-rich beetroot juice supplementation
new_entities.description: Beetroot juice used as a nitrate-rich ergogenic supplement before endurance exercise.

new_entities.name: Endurance time to exhaustion
aliases: time to exhaustion during endurance exercise
new_entities.description: How long an athlete or participant can maintain a set endurance workload before exhaustion.

edges.effect_quant: The earliest meta-analysis found a moderate pooled benefit for time-to-exhaustion outcomes, with effect size 0.79 (95% CI 0.23 to 1.35). But direct trials show that the signal is not uniform in trained populations: some studies extend endurance tolerance by roughly 15%, while others in elite endurance athletes show no improvement.
edges.population: healthy adults and trained endurance athletes taking nitrate-rich beetroot juice before endurance exercise
edges.mechanism: Dietary nitrate can increase nitric oxide bioavailability, lower the oxygen cost of submaximal work, and sometimes delay the point at which severe-intensity exercise becomes unsustainable. In highly trained athletes, however, the room for additional efficiency gains may be smaller, which is why the effect becomes more inconsistent.
edges.summary: Beetroot juice probably helps time-to-exhaustion performance in some endurance settings, but the athlete-specific literature is not cleanly one-directional. The most accurate interpretation is that the benefit is real on average, yet weaker and less reliable in elite endurance populations than in recreational or moderately trained participants.
edges.caveats: This edge is marked mixed because positive constant-load studies sit alongside null trials in high-level endurance athletes. It should not be read as proof that beetroot juice reliably improves every trained athlete's endurance test.

evidence.citation: HoonMW et al 2013 Int J Sport Nutr Exerc Metab
evidence.notes: The effect of nitrate supplementation on exercise performance in healthy individuals: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: nitrate supplementation versus control for time to exhaustion performance

evidence.citation: BaileySJ et al 2009 J Appl Physiol (1985)
evidence.notes: Dietary nitrate supplementation reduces the O2 cost of low-intensity exercise and enhances tolerance to high-intensity exercise in humans.
